'''Ann Esther Watkins''' is an American mathematician and statistician specializing in [[statistics education]]. She edited the ''[[College Mathematics Journal]]'' from 1989 to 1994, chaired the Advanced Placement Statistics Development Committee from 1997 to 1999,  and was president of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] from 2001 to 2002.{{r|profile|maapres|Rossman}}

Watkins is an emeritus professor of mathematics at [[California State University, Northridge]] (CSUN), her alma mater. She graduated from CSUN in 1970, and earned a master's degree there in 1972. She completed her Ph.D. in 1977 from the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].{{r|profile|em}}

With Richard L. Scheaffer, she is the author of statistics textbooks including
''Activity-Based Statistics'',
''Statistics: From Data to Decision'',
and ''Statistics in Action: Understanding a World of Data''.{{r|Rossman}}

She was elected as a [[fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1999 "for innovative contributions to curriculum and pedagogy; for masterful teaching, and teaching of teachers; and for an extraordinary record of sustained and successful efforts to institutionalize reform in statistics education."{{r|leitzel}} She won the United States Conference on Teaching Statistics Lifetime Achievement Award in 2015.{{r|Rossman|uscots}}
